prereg.rule_sheet: Adopt only if the preconditions hold (owner lifts the pins, vendored pinned copy, bundled advisories fixed or accepted) and D(with) >= 2/3 while D(without) <= 1/3, median false findings no higher, median total tokens <= 3x, measured always-on delta <= 1,500 tokens.

rule_first_stated.text: Stated up front. Preconditions independent of the runs: the owner accepts [features] plugins = true in setup.sh and agents-check and one MCP server for Codex; installs come only from a vendored pinned copy; and the bundled advisories (zod GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5, MCP SDK < 1.32.0, fast-uri < 3.1.9) are fixed upstream or accepted. If so, adopt codex-security only if D(with) holds in at least 2 of 3 runs while D(without) holds in at most 1 of 3, median F(with) <= median F(without), median T(with) <= 3x median T(without), and the measured always-on delta is <= 1,500 o200k tokens per session. If D(without) already holds in at least 2 of 3 runs, adopt only with equal D, F no higher and at least 25% fewer total tokens per run, counting the always-on delta. Otherwise: not adopted.

Every command was reviewed with 0007_cmd_review.py and 0007_hit_context.py: the calls read the repository's source and ran Python only on in-memory fixtures (patched reads, synthetic /proc text, synthetic jts.ini paths); none ran the lane or the probe, opened a socket, or named ~/Jts, a secret path, the main checkout, git fetch, git remote or 39cb68e. Web search: see web_search. Not contained (all three in owner_codex_home_writes): (1) the model runs in the owner's ~/.codex added to ~/.codex/config.toml a [projects."<clone path>"] table with the key trust_level for each clone they ran in (M1's wt/ctx, shared by its 3 runs, and wt/ab-0007-a-1, -a-2 and -a-3 under ~/src/meridian-ab/0007): 4 tables, counted on 2026-11-13 without printing values, each naming a clone since deleted. The file's time moved from 2026-11-12 21:33:38 ET (read by the re-check) to 2026-11-13 04:07:40 ET, a3's start. (2) Every run's thread went into Codex's state databases in that home: in state_5.sqlite 6 threads rows with the account-linked fields creator_account_id and creator_user_id set, and 6 thread_read_receipts rows; in thread_history_1.sqlite 74 thread_items rows, 6 thread_turns rows and 6 thread_history_projection_state rows. (3) 6 rollouts stay in ~/.codex/sessions (3 M1, a1, a2, a3). The rollouts carry account fields, and the same run data also sits in the database rows, so moving the rollouts alone leaves it behind. The home check compared names only, so it missed (1) and (2), and the measuring records' 'no owner file or policy changed' (first series) and 'No owner config, policy, main checkout or plugin state was touched' (second series) are wrong about config.toml and the two databases; those records are kept as written. with_window: A measuring window for codex-security would lift the plugins pin and adds only codex-security's stdio server to the empty [mcp_servers] allowlist (measure2.json what_would_have_to_change). It would keep apps pinned false, so no app connector (public-equity-investing's alpaca broker connector among them) and no install-suggestion tool loads. It turns remote_plugin off (on by default, policy_probe) in the window's throwaway CODEX_HOME, as [features] remote_plugin = false in that home's own config.toml (the pre-run method notes, method-codex, set it so for a plugin ADR), never in ~/.codex/config.toml; archiving that home's sessions/ and state/ and then deleting the home (the assessment's containment_check) undoes it, and restoring /etc/codex/requirements.toml undoes the [marketplaces] restriction below. It turns it off since with it on and the ChatGPT login the ChatGPT backend catalogue is active (remote_global_catalog_active = remote_plugin_enabled and an auth mode that uses the Codex backend, core-plugins/src/manager.rs 769-771 at ce21072). But with plugins on and that catalogue inactive, maybe_start_curated_repo_sync_for_config (manager.rs 774-790) starts the curated sync of openai/plugins main on every start (git ls-remote, then git fetch whenever main's head moved; start_curated_repo_sync, manager.rs 3381) unless MarketplacePolicy refuses the git source; with no [marketplaces] restrict_to_allowed_sources = true in the requirements the policy is unrestricted and validate_git_source passes (marketplace_policy.rs 55-62, 159-166), and the current /etc/codex/requirements.toml (meridian.user-data 68-77) has no [marketplaces] table. So the window also sets, in /etc/codex/requirements.toml, [marketplaces] restrict_to_allowed_sources = true with one [marketplaces.allowed_sources.<key>] entry, source = "local", for the vendored path only (the shape in marketplace_policy_tests.rs), which refuses the openai/plugins git source. Without it, the catalogue at upstream head (public-equity-investing and its alpaca connector included; apps = false still blocks the connector) becomes available, and only the installs, not the catalogue, stay limited to the vendored copy. Untested: the restriction, and the vendored route itself (refused under the policy, not verified to install with the pins lifted).
rerun: The scripts are records of what ran, not rerun harnesses (each header says so). 0007_r4_run.sh removes an existing run folder (rm -rf; for run name 1 that deletes a1's raw outputs) and keeps the old pgrep -f guard; both harnesses run codex exec in the owner's ~/.codex without the run-only trust flag, so each run wrote a trust_level table, thread rows and a rollout there (owner_codex_home_writes). Nothing watched a run while it lasted: the guard ran before setup and just before codex exec, and the agent then ran unsandboxed, with web search, for up to 60 minutes. M1 ran as: codex exec --json --color never -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort=high --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox -C "$WT" --disable hooks '<prompt>' < /dev/null. 0007_count_tokens.py reads OpenAI's o200k_base.tiktoken (the file tiktoken 0.14.0 pins, sha256 446a9538cb6c348e3516120d7c08b09f57c36495e2acfffe59a5bf8b0cfb1a2d) from --vocab-dir.
